text:
Rachel Kim: We need to get ahead of reference customer fatigue. Proposing we set hard guardrails before Sales starts blasting asks.

Miguel Santos: +1. I’ve already had 2 customers ask “how many of these calls are we signing up for?” and we don’t have a consistent answer.

Camila Reyes: Agree. For the design partner/reference program we should publish a default cap + a cooldown policy. What feels reasonable?

Avery Johnson: From the field side: we can live with a cap, but if it’s too low it’ll block late-stage deals. We need a path for exceptions.

Rachel Kim: Default cap suggestion: 2 reference calls / month / customer. Anything above requires CSM + customer approval (explicit) and we space them.

Miguel Santos: 2/mo feels ok for the “willing + public case study” folks. For more sensitive accounts (Helios type), I’d say 1/mo max.

Camila Reyes: Could we do a tiered system?
- Tier A (public logo + quotes): up to 2/mo
- Tier B (calls only, no public assets): 1/mo
- Tier C (security/compliance heavy): 1/qtr unless customer asks otherwise

Avery Johnson: That works if we can request an exception for a must-win enterprise deal. But exception should be clear and not surprise the customer.

Tyler Benson: If we do tiers I can add a HubSpot property + simple automation. Something like:
- Reference Tier: A/B/C
- Monthly Call Cap
- Cooldown Until (date)
And the intake form would show the cap + block scheduling if in cooldown.

Rachel Kim: Cooldown policy: after any reference call, minimum 14 days before next call. If customer says it was “a lot”, we can set 30 days.

Miguel Santos: I’d push for a default 21 days. The operational overhead (prep + follow up) is bigger than the 30 min call.

Camila Reyes: Ok: default cooldown 21 days, and we can set longer per customer. Also need opt-out language they can point to.

Michael Grant: Jumping in w/ legal hat. For opt-out language we should avoid anything that sounds like a contractual obligation to provide references. Keep it as “subject to availability” and “customer may decline any request.”

Rachel Kim: Yes. The whole point is customer-controlled.

Avery Johnson: Can we provide language Sales can use in emails? Something like “max 1–2 calls per month, you can always say no.”

Camila Reyes: Drafting suggested customer-facing language:
“Reference requests are optional and scheduled based on your availability. We’ll aim to limit requests to no more than 2 calls per month and will space calls by at least ~3 weeks. You can decline any request with no impact on support or service.”

Michael Grant: That’s good. Add a sentence that Redwood may pause requests at any time, and that customer can request a longer pause (cooldown).

Tyler Benson: Operationally: where do we capture “pause until”? We can store a date + a reason (travel, quarter-end, incident recovery).

Miguel Santos: Also need a “do not contact” toggle. Some customers are fine with one champion, but don’t want other teams pinging execs.

Rachel Kim: +1. DNC rules:
- Only CSM + designated AE can ask the customer for references
- Marketing never reaches out directly without CSM approval
- If a customer declines twice in a row, auto-cooldown 60 days

Avery Johnson: I’m ok with “declines twice => 60-day pause” as long as it’s clear the declines were true declines (vs “not this week”).

Tyler Benson: We can log outcome choices on the reference request record:
- Accepted
- Declined (timing)
- Declined (not comfortable)
- No response
Only “Declined (not comfortable)” triggers the long cooldown.

Miguel Santos: Perfect. Timing decline shouldn’t penalize them.

Camila Reyes: What should the actual caps be? Can we land on:
- Tier A: 2 calls/month, 21-day cooldown
- Tier B: 1 call/month, 21-day cooldown
- Tier C: 1 call/quarter, 30-day cooldown
Exceptions: requires CSM approval + explicit customer confirmation.

Rachel Kim: Works. But I want a maximum number per quarter even for Tier A. Otherwise 2/mo = 6/qtr and that’s still heavy.

Avery Johnson: Hmm. We don’t usually hit 6, but fair. Maybe “up to 4 per quarter”?

Miguel Santos: 4/qtr max for Tier A seems reasonable.

Michael Grant: Keep the internal caps internal. Customer-facing should remain “we aim to limit…” not “you agree to…”

Camila Reyes: Makes sense. Customer-facing copy can be softer; internal tooling enforces the cap.

Tyler Benson: I’ll implement:
- Tier A: cap 2/mo AND 4/qtr
- Tier B: 1/mo AND 2/qtr
- Tier C: 1/qtr
Cooldown Until = call_date + 21 days (or 30 days for Tier C / custom)
Also adding “Reference Status: Active / Paused / Opted out”.

Rachel Kim: Define “Opted out” = no asks without them re-opting in. “Paused” = temporary.

Avery Johnson: How do we handle must-win exceptions? We should avoid putting CSM in a bad spot.

Rachel Kim: Exception flow:
1) AE submits request w/ deal context (stage, value, why this customer)
2) CSM confirms relationship health + customer capacity
3) If approved, CSM asks customer “are you open to one additional call this month?”
If customer says no, it’s a no. No escalation to exec.

Miguel Santos: Please add “no escalation” in the playbook. Customers hate being pressured.

Camila Reyes: +1. I’ll add it to the Confluence intake doc + include wording for “soft no” handling.

Michael Grant: Also recommend we add a sentence to the consent form draft that participation is voluntary and can be revoked at any time. (It’s probably already there but make sure.)

Camila Reyes: It is in v2, but I’ll double-check the exact clause.

Tyler Benson: Action items:
- I’ll add HubSpot fields + validation rules
- Rachel: can you write the exact cooldown/cap policy text for CS enablement?
- Camila: update playbook + outreach snippets

Rachel Kim: Yep. I’ll post a policy draft here today.

Avery Johnson: Thanks all. This will help a ton with setting expectations in deal cycles.

Miguel Santos: And keep us from burning our best customers :)

Rachel Kim: Posting draft CS policy text (v0.1) for review:
“Reference participation is optional. Default limits:
- Tier A (public story): up to 2 calls/month, max 4/quarter; min 21 days between calls
- Tier B (calls only): up to 1 call/month, max 2/quarter; min 21 days between calls
- Tier C (sensitive/compliance): up to 1 call/quarter; min 30 days between calls
Customers may decline any request. If a customer expresses discomfort, set Reference Status = Paused (60 days) or Opted Out. No escalation path if customer declines.”

Michael Grant: Looks good. Suggest minor tweak: “If a customer expresses discomfort” -> “If a customer declines due to discomfort or requests a pause”.

Camila Reyes: Works. I’ll incorporate and align language with the consent form + marketing copy.

Tyler Benson: Once we align, I’ll pin this in #customer-success and add it to the intake form helper text.

Rachel Kim: Done. Please also make sure Sales sees the cap in the request form so we stop getting last-minute pings.

Avery Johnson: :thumbsup: I’ll reinforce with the AE team that we need lead time + respect cooldown.

Miguel Santos: Great. Closing loop after Tyler updates HubSpot.
